title: Acid diluted a thousandfold
hook: Diluting a strong acid tenfold raises its pH by about one. What does a thousandfold do?

knows: that each pH unit is a factor of 10 in hydrogen ions (ph-log-scale)
doesNotKnow: that water makes its own H+ and OH- (about 10^-7 mol/L each at 25 °C)
that diluting an acid therefore stalls near pH 7 instead of passing it

misconception: Diluting 10 times always raises the pH by 1, so a pH 5 acid diluted 1,000 times becomes pH 8 (basic).
objective: The learner can explain that a pH 5 acid diluted 1,000 times ends near pH 6.98, not 8, because water's own ions (10^-7 mol/L at 25 °C) take over as the acid's share falls, and that adding water cannot make an acid basic.

claims.text: Diluting a strong acid tenfold raises its pH by about one, while the acid's H+ is well above water's own 10^-7 mol/L (hook; stage: ×1 to ×10 goes from pH 5.00 to 6.00).
claims.source: pH = -log10(c) for a fully dissociated strong acid when c >> 10^-7 mol/L; with c/10 the pH rises by log10(10) = 1. The formula in c3 gives 5.00 -> 6.00 for x10 (node). The hook's qualifier is 'strong acid'; the lesson then shows where it fails.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Derivation re-run in node with my own bisection on the charge balance h = c + Kw/h (not the lesson's closed form; scratch acid.mjs): x1 pH 5.0000, x10 pH 5.9957, shown 6.00. pH = -log10(c) when c >> 1e-7, so tenfold dilution adds 1. Hook qualifier 'strong acid' rests on c4 (verified).

claims.text: At 25 °C the ion product of water is [H+][OH−] = about 10^-14, and water splits into equal amounts of H+ and OH−, so neutral water holds about 10^-7 mol/L of each, and pure water at 25 °C is pH 7 (stage line 'pH 7 neutral'; reveal: 'Water splits into equal H⁺ and OH⁻, and at 25 °C [H⁺] × [OH⁻] stays 10⁻¹⁴ ... water's share grew toward 10⁻⁷ mol/L each: pH 7').
claims.source: CRC Handbook, 'Ionization constant of water as a function of temperature and pressure' (pKw = 13.99-14.00 at 25 °C); Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry. Brief claim 1.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): reveal wording changed (learner r10); previously unverified. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Opened source: the IAPWS R11-07 ionization-constant formulation as implemented in PyPI iapws 1.5.5 (_Kw), at 298.15 K and 0.101325 MPa (rho 997.05 kg/m^3 from IAPWS-95): pKw = 13.994, so Kw = 1.01e-14, 'about 10^-14'. Equal H+ and OH- from water alone (charge balance) gives sqrt(Kw) = 1.0e-7 mol/L each, pH 7.00. Reveal wording ('Water splits into equal H⁺ and OH⁻, and at 25 °C [H⁺] × [OH⁻] stays 10⁻¹⁴') matches.

claims.text: A pH 5 hydrochloric acid diluted 1,000 times with pure water has pH about 6.98 (the acid supplies 1.0 x 10^-8 mol/L of H+, water itself about 9.5 x 10^-8), and one more tenfold reaches only 7.00 (stage bars and readouts 'pH at ×1,000 6.98', 'pH at ×10,000 7.00'; reveal: 'At 1,000-fold dilution your pH stopped at 6.98, not 8, and one more tenfold reached only 7.00').
claims.source: Charge balance [H+] = c + [OH−] with [H+][OH−] = Kw = 1.0e-14 gives [H+] = c/2 + sqrt(c^2/4 + Kw); water's own H+ equals [OH−] = Kw/[H+] (water ionises in pairs). c = 1e-8: [H+] = 1.051e-7, pH 6.978, water 9.51e-8 (ratio 9.5, 'about ten times'); c = 1e-9: pH 6.998, shown as 7.00. x10: 5.996, x100: 6.791 (node, demo-builder 2026-10-14; Demo.tsx solve()). Brief claim 2.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Derivation re-run in node with an independent bisection solver: x1,000 pH 6.9783 (shown 6.98), acid 1.0e-8, water 9.512e-8; x10,000 pH 6.9978 (shown 7.00); x100 6.791. Matches Demo.tsx solve() and the stage readouts. Rests on Kw (c2) and full dissociation (c4), both verified.

claims.text: Hydrochloric acid at these concentrations is fully dissociated.
claims.source: Atkins & de Paula, or any general chemistry text: HCl is a strong acid (pKa about −6), fully dissociated in dilute solution. Not stated to the learner; it underlies c3. Brief claim 3.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Opened OpenStax Chemistry 2e section 4.2 (m68710): 'Virtually every HCl molecule that dissolves in water will undergo this reaction ... called strong acids', HCl in the 'Common Strong Acids' table; section 11.2 (m68781): 'essentially 100% complete for HCl'. Applies a fortiori at 1e-5 to 1e-9 mol/L. The cited pKa -6 was not checked and is not shown to learners.

claims.text: Assumption: 'pure water' means CO2-free water at 25 °C (question says 'pure water at 25 °C'); water left open to air absorbs CO2 and is slightly acidic. The lesson quotes no pH for air-saturated water.
claims.note: FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Convention, stated in the question ('pure water at 25 °C'). The factual half ('water left open to air absorbs CO2 and is slightly acidic') checked in OpenStax Chemistry 2e section 14.2 (m68804): 'Normal rainwater has a pH between 5 and 6 due to the presence of dissolved CO2 which forms carbonic acid'.

claims.text: Adding pure water to an acid brings it toward pH 7 but never past it, because water adds equal amounts of H+ and OH− (reveal: 'water's share grew toward 10⁻⁷ mol/L each: pH 7, never past it'; stage: the total bar stops at the pH 7 line). Dilution does move pH (reveal line shown to a learner who chose 'about 5').
claims.source: From the charge balance in c3: [H+] = c + [OH−] >= [OH−] for any c >= 0, so [H+] >= 10^-7 and pH <= 7 at 25 °C; as c -> 0, pH -> 7.00 from below (x100,000: 7.000). Brief claim 5.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): reveal wording changed (learner r10); previously unverified. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Derivation: charge balance [H+] = c + [OH-] >= [OH-] with [H+][OH-] = Kw gives [H+] >= 1e-7, pH <= 7; own python with solve()'s formula: pH 5.000, 5.996, 6.791, 6.978, 6.998, 7.000 at x1 ... x100,000. 'pH 7, never past it' holds; 'Dilution does move pH' (shown to a learner who picked 'about 5') holds.

claims.text: On the bars, the water's share of the H+ grows as the acid's shrinks; the reveal quotes the ratio on the stage when it opens, e.g. at ×10,000 water itself supplies about 100 times more H+ than the acid, at ×1,000 about 9.5 times (reveal: 'On your bars now (×10,000), water itself supplies 100 times more H⁺ than the acid'; 'As the acid thinned, water's share grew').
claims.source: Water's H+ = Kw/[H+]: 1.0e-9 (x1), 9.9e-9 (x10), 6.2e-8 (x100), 9.5e-8 (x1,000), 9.95e-8 (x10,000), while the acid's falls 1e-5 to 1e-9 (node; Demo.tsx solve(), ratio rounded to 2 significant figures: 99.5 -> 100, 9.51 -> 9.5). Below x100 the acid supplies more (x10: about 100 times more). The acid at higher concentration suppresses water's own ionisation (common-ion effect, Le Chatelier); not named on stage.
claims.note: Reset to unverified by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14): reveal wording changed (learner r10); previously unverified. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Own python: water's H+ = Kw/[H+] = 1.0e-9, 9.9e-9, 6.18e-8, 9.51e-8, 9.95e-8 at x1, x10, x100, x1,000, x10,000 against the acid's 1e-5 ... 1e-9. Ratios to 2 s.f.: x10,000 99.5 -> 100; x1,000 9.51 -> 9.5; x10 acid 101x more -> 100. The reveal computes the ratio from the stage's current dilution with toPrecision(2).

claims.text: In strong acid the H+ squeezes OH− down (product fixed at 10^-14), and water's own H+ comes paired with that OH−, so water's bar starts tiny: at pH 5 water supplies about 1.0 x 10^-9 mol/L of H+ (reveal: 'Strong acid squeezes OH⁻ down, and water's H⁺ comes paired with it, so water's bar started tiny').
claims.source: Charge and mass balance for strong acid c in water: [H+] = c/2 + sqrt(c^2/4 + Kw), water's share = [OH−] = Kw/[H+]. Builder node re-run 2026-10-14 (Kw = 1e-14): water H+ 1.00e-9, 9.90e-9, 6.18e-8, 9.51e-8, 9.95e-8 mol/L at x1, x10, x100, x1,000, x10,000; pH 5.00, 6.00, 6.79, 6.98, 7.00. Textbook common-ion effect on water autoionisation (e.g. Atkins, Chemical Principles); source not opened by the builder.
claims.note: Added by demo-builder (W-839, 2026-10-14); needs the fact-checker. | FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Derivation as c7: [H+] = c/2 + sqrt(c^2/4 + Kw), water's share = [OH-] = Kw/[H+]; at pH 5 (c = 1e-5) water supplies 1.0e-9 mol/L. Strong acid holds [OH-] down because the product is fixed, so water's paired H+ starts tiny. The common-ion name is not on the stage, so no source is needed for it.

recall.question: You keep adding pure water to a little vinegar. What does its pH approach?
options: It keeps rising past 7 and the solution turns basic
It approaches 7 but stays just below it
recall.why: Water makes its own H+ and OH- in equal amounts (10^-7 mol/L each at 25 °C). As the acid's share shrinks, water's ions take over, so the pH creeps toward 7 but never passes it.
